public_rationale: On the ordinary reading of 'at all,' the 2021 BART and T5 study provides a counterexample. It found structured representations of changing entity states and tested their influence on generation. Prediction and internal state representation can therefore coexist. This does not establish complete, reliable human-like world models. The result depends on including these language models and accepting limited state representations as representations of the world.
limitations: BART and T5 differ from GPT-style decoder-only models.
The experiments concern simple domains and include task fine-tuning.
The study reports errors and leaves richer world representations unresolved.

our_interpretation: Assess the empirical assertion about model representations, not the authors' private state of knowledge.
The plain reading of 'at all' excludes even limited, repeatable representations of entities and their changing states. It does not require a complete or infallible model of reality.
Next-word prediction is a training or output task; the relevant question is whether internal representations support that task.

The target is the stock of model capabilities available as of 22 June 2022. There is no regular reporting period for this capability claim and no stated beginning; pre-existing models remain in scope, while later-created models do not.
criteria.support_condition: Appropriate probing and intervention studies of the relevant models establish that apparent state tracking does not depend on repeatable internal representations of entities and situations.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A model available by the post date demonstrably encodes structured entity or situation states, with controls and interventions showing more than superficial word associations.
